passage:
Tom's uncle opened a small noodle shop. On the first day, Tom helped clean tables and bring water to customers. But for the first hour, no one came.
His uncle did not look worried. He checked the soup, cut vegetables, and smiled.
At noon, an old woman entered. She ordered one bowl of noodles and ate slowly. Before leaving, she said, "The soup tastes like the noodles I had when I was young."
Tom's uncle wrote those words on a piece of paper and taped it near the kitchen.
Many customers came in later that week, but Tom's uncle always remembered the first one. He said a business starts with money, but it grows with trust.
